subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled:false` become a hard read/exec access boundary, or should disabled-skill visibility remain separate from an explicit filesystem/exec security policy?
rationale: This is a public config semantic and security boundary choice with compatibility risk; source inspection shows the current behavior is visibility filtering, while the requested behavior would cross filesystem tools, exec, sandbox, Gateway/UI, and docs.

options.title: Design explicit skill access policy
options.body: Keep this issue open, decide the contract, and implement a central policy that names whether disabled skills deny reads, writes, exec, sandbox sync, or only prompt exposure.

options.title: Keep `enabled:false` as visibility only
options.body: Document the current meaning and route hard filesystem/exec isolation to a separate `tools.fs` or sandbox policy such as the broader filesystem-boundary tracker.

options.title: Make `enabled:false` a hard deny now
options.body: Treat the existing flag as the security boundary and require upgrade notes, compatibility tests, and explicit coverage for shell-mediated access before landing.

recommendation.title: Design explicit skill access policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, decide the contract, and implement a central policy that names whether disabled skills deny reads, writes, exec, sandbox sync, or only prompt exposure.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest available security-direction and adjacent skills/sandbox review history for this cross-cutting boundary choice.
